reuse.why: Reuses findOrCreateBank, syncAccount, handleSyncResponse, post/BankSyncError and introduces one shared guard for all link handlers, but re-types unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it and adds Fintegra by copying instead of factoring the near-identical link/download functions.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near-verbatim copy of linkSimpleFinAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions, and the detach loop copies unlinkAccount's updateAccount block.

placement.why: Guard lives in accounts/app.ts next to the link handlers, download function in sync.ts, server URL in server-config.ts and type in types/models, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the four requested behaviours plus release notes; the guard folding the closed-account rule and unlinking into one function is the only stretch.

maintainability.why: A single guard called by every link handler is good, but a function named assert... that also mutates (unlinks previous holders) and checks closed state is surprising, and a sixth copied provider function grows the copy burden.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All link handlers route through assertBankAccountNotLinked; the detach loop re-implements unlinkAccount's reset (unlinkAccount is a handler with GoCardless side effects, so not directly callable), counted as duplication rather than bypass.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (linkFintegraAccount vs linkSimpleFinAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions vs downloadAkahuTransactions, detach reset vs unlinkAccount) are plain, recognisable copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts: step 4 adds replaceExistingLink and the detach loop (side effects inside an assert), step 3 adds the closed-account branch plus an odd '!target && existing.length > 0' not-found branch; all six link handlers call it.
